statement: The Board is told of every personal data breach, with no harm or size threshold, without delay on becoming aware of it, describing its nature, extent, timing, location and likely impact. A detailed report follows within 72 hours of becoming aware, or within a longer period the Board allows on a written request. The report uses the prescribed form and covers the facts and causes, mitigation, who caused it, steps to prevent recurrence and the notices sent to data principals. Proof is the breach procedure, the report template and the submission records.
why_asked: Missing or late reports to the regulator are penalized separately from the breach itself, and teams often wait for certainty before reporting.
how_to_ask: Ask what triggers the first report and who sends it, then ask for the detailed report template. Check recent breaches against the times. Example probe: "For your last breach, show me when you became aware, when the Board was told and when the detailed report went in."
question: Does your organization report every personal data breach to the Board on time, in the prescribed form?
expected_evidence: Breach procedure with Board reporting steps; Board report template; incident log; Board submission records with dates, for the audit period.
good_looks_like: The procedure requires immediate initial notice for every breach, with no harm threshold, and a detailed report within 72 hours. The template covers every required element. Records show both reports reached the Board on time.
test: Sample personal data breaches from the audit period. Compare the time of awareness with the dates of the initial notice and the detailed report. Pass if every sampled breach has both on time and the report contains the template content.
baseline_risk: The regulator is not told of a breach in time, which adds a separate penalty and erodes trust.
key_settings: dpdpa: notify the Board without delay on becoming aware of a personal data breach | dpdpa: send the detailed report to the Board within 72 hours of becoming aware, or within a longer period the Board allows on a written request

statement: Each data principal affected by a personal data breach is notified without delay, through the user account or a communication channel the person registered. The notice is in clear, plain language and covers the nature, extent and timing of the breach, its likely consequences for the person, the mitigation taken, the steps the person can take and a contact for questions. This applies to every affected person with no harm threshold. Proof is the notification template and the dispatch records.
why_asked: People cannot protect themselves from a breach they do not know about, and a notice that is vague or late leaves them exposed.
how_to_ask: Ask how affected people are identified and reached, then ask for the notice template and a sent notice. Example probe: "Show me the notice sent to people in your last breach and how you chose who got it."
question: Does your organization notify each data principal affected by a personal data breach without delay?
expected_evidence: Breach procedure for individual notices; notification template; incident log; notification dispatch records for the audit period.
good_looks_like: The procedure identifies each affected person and notifies them without delay through the account or a registered channel. The template covers all required content in plain language, and dispatch records match the affected list.
test: Sample personal data breaches from the audit period. Compare the affected list with the dispatch records and check the notice content against the template. Pass if every affected person in each sampled breach was notified without delay with the required content.
baseline_risk: Affected individuals are not told in time, so they cannot take steps to protect themselves.

statement: A register records every personal data breach with the facts, the effects, the remedial actions and the dates the Board and the affected data principals were notified. Each breach is added to the register as it is confirmed, and the register is checked against the security incident log on a defined cycle. Proof is the register and the reconciliation records.
why_asked: Without one register, the facts the regulator may ask for are scattered and some breaches never get recorded at all.
how_to_ask: Ask to see the register and compare it with the security incident log. Example probe: "Show me a breach from your incident log and its entry in the breach register."
question: Does your organization keep a register of every personal data breach with its facts, effects and remedial actions?
expected_evidence: Breach register; security incident log and tickets; reconciliation records of register against log, for the audit period.
good_looks_like: Every confirmed breach has an entry with facts, effects, remedial actions and the notification dates for the Board and data principals. The register matches the security incident log.
test: Take the personal data breaches from the security incident log for the audit period and look each up in the register. Pass if every breach appears with facts, effects, remedial actions and both notification dates.
baseline_risk: Breaches go unrecorded, so the organization cannot show the regulator what happened or what it did.
